There is a potential drop of 7 V across L and a further 4 V potential drop across N.
What are the potential drops across M, P and Q?

hints: Notice the labelled nodes: L joins the left + node A to the top-middle node B with a $7\text{ V}$ drop, and N joins B to the bottom-middle node C with a $4\text{ V}$ drop.
Recall Kirchhoff's second law: around any closed loop the potential drops must balance the $20\text{ V}$ rise, and components connected between the same two nodes have the same potential difference.
Compare P with the L plus N route between A and C, then compare M between B and the - terminal with the $7\text{ V}$ plus $20\text{ V}$ route, and Q between C and the - terminal similarly.
walkthrough: Label the left junction A at supply +, the top-middle junction B, the bottom-middle junction C, and the right junction D at supply -. Then $V_A-V_B=7\text{ V}$, $V_B-V_C=4\text{ V}$ and $V_A-V_D=20\text{ V}$.
Resistor P connects A directly to C, in parallel with the series route L plus N. By Kirchhoff's law, $V_P=(V_A-V_B)+(V_B-V_C)=7\text{ V}+4\text{ V}=11\text{ V}$.

Resistor M connects B directly to D. Going B to A to D gives a $7\text{ V}$ rise then a $20\text{ V}$ drop, so the B to D drop is $V_M=20\text{ V}-7\text{ V}=13\text{ V}$. Algebraically $V_B-V_D=(V_A-7)-(V_A-20)=13\text{ V}$.

Resistor Q connects C directly to D. Going C to A to D gives an $11\text{ V}$ rise then a $20\text{ V}$ drop, so $V_Q=20\text{ V}-11\text{ V}=9\text{ V}$. Algebraically $V_C-V_D=(V_A-11)-(V_A-20)=9\text{ V}$.
Thus the drops are M $=13\text{ V}$, P $=11\text{ V}$, Q $=9\text{ V}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Gives $9\text{ V}$ for M and $13\text{ V}$ for Q, which swaps the $13\text{ V}$ and $9\text{ V}$ drops from the B-D and C-D branches.

B.explanation: Gives $7\text{ V}$ for P, which ignores the $4\text{ V}$ drop across N in series with the $7\text{ V}$ drop across L between the same two nodes.

C.explanation: Gives $13\text{ V}$, $11\text{ V}$ and $9\text{ V}$, which satisfy Kirchhoff's second law for the L-N-P loop and the loops containing the $20\text{ V}$ supply.

D.explanation: Gives $17\text{ V}$ and $3\text{ V}$ values that do not make the drops around the L-M-supply loop and N-Q-M loop sum correctly.
